points.text: Application control is only part of the Trustworthy software outcome. Software also needs to be supported, verified and approved by the organisation.
Admin and management tools need to be limited to approved sets and run only from authorised locations.
Exceptions need to be minimised, formally risk-accepted, time-limited, monitored and reviewed regularly.
Trustworthy software applies across all technical domains, so check that existing controls cover each relevant domain.

source.location: "Where investment(s) may need to be strengthened", page 12

points.text: Asset records need to cover infrastructure, operating systems, applications, identities, credentials and data as separate assets, so existing inventories may need to grow.
Patching should take into account how exploitable, exposed and critical a vulnerability is, its impact and any compensating controls. ISM, regulatory and other mandatory timeframes still apply.
The right treatment timeframe may differ between domains because their assets and risks differ.
Where legacy systems can't be removed or replaced straight away, their risk needs to be identified and managed until they are.

source.location: "Where investment(s) may need to be strengthened", page 13

points.text: MFA is only one part of Identity, credential and access management. Also needed: removing default and unused accounts, storing keys and secrets securely, scanning for exposed credentials, turning off legacy authentication protocols, and unique credentials per account.
Check MFA coverage in each relevant domain, not just for external or remote access.

source.location: "Where investment(s) may need to be strengthened", page 14

points.text: Identify which assets and functions make up the Privileged environments domain, including management platforms and privileged access services.
Privileged actions need explicit session controls, including time-limited grants. Organisations with standing admin access should check whether they meet this.
Logs need to capture admin actions that change systems, configurations or controls, including who, when and what.
Least privilege applies to service and other non-person accounts as well as user accounts.
Lateral movement needs to be limited to explicitly approved pathways and services, based on business need and trust level.

source.location: "Where investment(s) may need to be strengthened", page 16

points.text: Macro controls are part of a broader need to control software execution. Consider equivalent controls for other ways code can run.
Macro settings should be part of approved configuration baselines that are deployed, maintained and reviewed.
Processes are needed to detect and fix configuration drift, using scheduled checks and, where possible, automated monitoring.

source.location: "Where investment(s) may need to be strengthened", page 17

points.text: Configuration baselines should suit the environment and be formally approved and maintained.
Deviations from approved baselines need to be detected and fixed.
Baselines should cover the relevant assets in each applicable domain.
Secure configuration management applies across all technical domains, not only endpoints.
Blocking ads and browser content may help with Content filtering, but outbound connections across all relevant applications and services need to be considered.

source.location: "Where investment(s) may need to be strengthened", page 18

points.text: Backup storage needs to be secure and resilient, for example encrypted and immutable, offline, logically isolated or similar.
Backup repositories need to be separated from primary systems, user environments and production workloads, so an attacker can't damage both.
Restore testing should show that recovery time and recovery point objectives can be met.
Check that backups cover the important data, applications and settings for each applicable domain.

source.location: "Where investment(s) may need to be strengthened", page 20

strengthen.topic: Visibility and response across all phases
strengthen.text: Visibility and response applies in every priority phase and grows as more domains are implemented.
High-value security logs and configuration changes need to be forwarded to central logging, and logs need to support correlation across systems.
Detection should cover unauthorised changes, unusual sign-in activity, suspicious software execution and other behaviour relevant to the domains in scope.
Detection coverage should be reviewed to find gaps from new assets, services, threats or architecture changes.
Incident response procedures need to be documented, tested and approved.
Reviews should identify the gaps that enabled an incident and whether monitoring and response need to change.

source.location: Event logging, detection and response, pages 20-21
